creator: youraveragetechbro
title: Two home-made skills, /phased-plan and phase-implementation: plans are split into tiny user-testable phases and the AI may not start the next phase until the human reviews and approves, to avoid 10,000-line PRs

tools.name: /phased-plan skill
tools.detail: Creator-authored Claude Code / Codex skill; forces every plan phase to be a small chunk testable from both client and backend

tools.name: phase-implementation skill
tools.detail: Tells the AI to implement only one phase, then stop until the human reviews and says go

claims: Writing code is no longer the limiting factor; the reviewer's mental bandwidth is
Each phase must be user-testable from the client side and the backend side
Result: far fewer gigantic 10,000-line PRs, smaller PRs, cleaner git history
Works for both Claude Code and Codex
how_to_steps: Create a /phased-plan skill that instructs the model to break a feature plan into very small phases, each independently testable by a user end to end
Create a phase-implementation skill that restricts the model to one phase at a time and requires explicit human approval before continuing
Review and approve each phase, producing one small PR per phase
on_screen_only: Title text 'my most used Claude Code/Codex Skill'; caption shows the slash command as '/phased-plan'
cta: Watch the linked video on his other AI coding skills (no comment/DM ask)

relevance.why: Directly addresses a time-poor solo founder's bottleneck: reviewing what Claude wrote. Two tiny skills enforce vertical slices with a human gate, cutting review load and regressions.

implement_score.why: Write two SKILL.md files in ~20 minutes (phase planning rules + 'stop after one phase and wait for approval'); no dependencies. Compose with the existing /plan-/build-style commands already in the liked set.

verify: The skills are not published in the video; a researcher must write their own or find them on the creator's channel
Check that 'stop and wait for approval' actually holds in Claude Code auto/accept-edits modes (model may continue unless the skill is firm)
Measure whether phase size reduces total tokens or increases them via repeated context reloads

gap.what: Liked set has ordered command packs (/spec /plan /build) and verification skills, but not the technique of forcing every plan phase to be a user-testable vertical slice with a hard human approval gate between phases.
